HomePage.title: Future Steps
HomePage.subtitle: A community platform designing, executing, and documenting youth-led development initiatives — turning ideas into measurable impact.

about.label: About
about.title: Not built for one initiative
about.description: Future Steps is a digital platform bringing together multiple community initiatives, documenting each one's full lifecycle — from idea to impact — under one transparent standard. Every initiative gets an official documentation ID, measurable KPIs, and a full audit trail.

ChildLearning.title: Teaching Camp Children How to Prompt the Machine
ChildLearning.description: An educational initiative in Gaza displacement camps training children in tech basics, AI, and prompt engineering — with simple tools, short curricula, and instructors from within the camp.

prompt.label: 01 - PROMPT
prompt.text: "Explain how a solar cell works in words a ten-year-old child can understand"

output.label: 02 - OUTPUT
output.text: An answer the child understands – learning how to frame the question to get it.

ChildLearning.promptNote: The first lesson is not coding. The first lesson is asking the right question.

items.question: Does the child need a private device?
items.answer: No, available devices are shared in small groups under the supervision of a local teacher inside the camp.

items.question: What is the age group?
items.answer: The track is designed for children aged 10 to 14 in displacement camps.

items.question: How is financial support spent?
items.answer: Support is dedicated to providing basic tools, training supplies, and incentives for local teachers.

items.question: Can I volunteer remotely?
items.answer: Yes, through curriculum review, translation, and teacher training via recorded sessions. Direct teaching remains local.

intro.label: 01 — WHAT IT IS
intro.title: Not a coding course. A way of thinking.
intro.description: In displacement camps, electricity is unreliable, internet access is limited, and devices are scarce. We built the curriculum around this reality, not against it: short sessions, offline-friendly content, and shared devices. We are not teaching one particular tool — we are teaching children how to frame a question, read an answer, and judge it.

phases.title: Curiosity
phases.description: How does a computer think? Screenless logic games before the first device.

phases.title: The Question
phases.description: Prompt engineering: formulation, refinement, and clarity. The difference between a vague question and a precise one.

phases.title: Judgment
phases.description: When does the machine get things wrong? Exercises in verifying information before believing it.

phases.title: The Project
phases.description: A story, simple game, or illustrated guide — created by the child and showcased to the camp.

promptTerminal.prompt: Describe a garden that grows on the roof of our school.
promptTerminal.result: Tomato vines climb the water tanks. Solar panels open like leaves. Every child waters one row.
